title: Mark Stephens (Eskenazi Health Security)

communications.subject: Indiana Access to Public Records Act Request: Mark Stephens (Eskenazi Health Security)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Indiana Access to Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records related to the following current or former employees:

Mark Stephens (5347-3087)

Hiring date, termination date, compensation, commendations, assignments/job roles, disciplinary actions, factual basis for disciplinary actions and letters of resignation for the following employees. Please exclude copies of individual training certificates.

I am including the following information as a helpful reference to related case law and Public Access Counselor opinions regarding personnel records of public employees:

https://public.courts.in.gov/Decisions/api/Document/Opinion?Id=QPNIyLTvnhzxDZhO52J1KCEs4fPOKpLR0hAitsADZUhV--IpFNWE224Cxiw0N3jJ0

Indiana Supreme Court decision WTHR-TV v. Hamilton Southeastern School District states that APRA requires disclosure of the factual basis for disciplinary action, and that factual basis cannot be a bald conclusion. It also has to be sufficient for a reasonable person to understand what an employee did to deserve discipline. See the opinion starting on page 7 of the link above.

A passing reference to violation of a specific policy is not sufficient to meet this standard.

The Indiana Public Access Counselor also has addressed the topic of resignations in lieu of termination. One such opinion can be reviewed here, but simply put a resignation in lieu of a termination does not dissolve an agency’s responsibility to provide the factual basis for discipline under the public records statute.

The state’s records statute applies to all employees, regardless of wither they are probationary or not.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 7 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Emily Hopkins

communications.subject: Wyoming Public Records Act Request: Contract Request: Interfolio (University of Wyoming)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Wyoming Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

The most recent contract, governing, base, or master license agreement with Elsevier relating to the licensing of Interfolio;
All related terms and conditions, terms of service, amendments, addenda, appendices, attachments, product terms, MOUs, MOAs, and/or data processing agreements; 
All financial documents or records of financial transactions, exchanges or obligations related to the contractual relations with Elsevier for faculty information system technology;
and
Assessment documentation such as the Higher Education Community Vendor Assessment Toolkit (HECVAT) related to Interfolio. 

Responsive materials include all contracts, agreements, amendments, appendices, invoices, and any other documents listed above that incorporate language governing terms of use of Interfolio.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 7 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Michele Gibney

title: Flock Safety System Usage and Cost Information (Plano Police Department)

communications.subject: Texas Public Information Act Request: Flock Safety System Usage and Cost Information (Plano Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Texas Public Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. Audit logs dating back to January 1, 2026 for searches of any part of the Flock Safety system dating from the initial contract by government employees, private entities operating on behalf of the government, and/or unauthorized searches of the system by any party.

2. Official policy documents that show when and how the Flock Safety system may and/or may not be used.

3. Records of all alleged occurances of nonpermissible searches of Flock Safety systems to include the search criteria, the system(s) searched, the name of the individual that made the search, the stated reason(s) for the search, the current employment status of the one(s) alleged to have misused the system, and a copy of all disciplinary proceedings and the disposition of such proceedings that occurred as a result of the alleged misuse of the system.

4. A list of all criminal charges filed on or after January 1, 2026 where the data from Flock Safety has been admitted into evidence. This list need only include the venue for the case, the docket number, the associated law enforcement agency, the agency's case number(s) associated with the charges, the date the case was filed,  and the disposition status of the case (if available).

5. Financial records that disclose the amount of money disbursed to Flock Safety, Inc. since January 1, 2026.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. Given the volume of this records request, I would prefer the request filled electronically by USB flash drive if available, or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Nicholas Squires

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Information about the lease of DCR land by Tufts University (Division Of Capital Asset Management And Maintenance)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

The current and all prior leases, permits, licenses, occupancy agreements, or other agreements between the Commonwealth/DCR (or its predecessor MDC) and Tufts University concerning the Tufts University sailing facility/boathouse now known as the Lawrence S. and Adele Fleet Bacow Sailing Pavilion at Upper Mystic Lake, approximately 1600 Mystic Valley Parkway, including all exhibits, plans, surveys, amendments, extensions, renewals, and documents defining public-access obligations or the boundaries of the premises.

I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, and is not made for commercial usage.

I expect the request to be filled in an accessible format, including for screen readers, which provide text-to-speech for persons unable to read print. Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf image files as well as physical documents.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Daniel Jalkut

communications.subject: RE: Washington Public Records Act Request #W038512-080926
communications.communication:
Thank you.

Within the Fusus system, users can see cameras that are owned or leased by other police or private groups which are shared to your department. Fusus describes these as "donor" cameras.

communications.subject: Police Record Request :: W038512-080926
communications.communication:
--- City of Redmond --- 
 RE: PUBLIC RECORDS REQUEST of 8/9/2026, Reference # W038512-080926 
Dear e e, 
The Redmond Police Records Division received your correspondence on August 12th, 2026. Thank you so much for the clarification, Redmond does not have any "donor" cameras. All mounted cameras in our Fusus system are City of Redmond Cameras, the only exception to mounted cameras being our DFR Drones which only provide a live feed if they are in flight. In the spread sheet provided in the first installment  please note that column B/ Disposition has a value of "1" or "2"; the value of "1" means a camera is "internal" meaning it is mounted on the inside of a building and "2" is an external camera meaning it is mounted on the outside of a building or traffic pole. The column L/sharing status will have a value of yes or no, if it is yes it means that we share that traffic camera live feed with GIS Map. The rest of the columns in the spreadsheet should be self explanatory, however let us know if you have any questions. 
In accordance with RCW 42.56.520, we are notifying you that additional time is required to process your request due to the records needing to be pulled from a different city department and our need to prioritize other essential government functions. We will process this request in installments (RCW 42.56.120 / WAC 44-14-07006).  The first installment of a list of the cameras contributing to our Fuses platform is provided the e to your request is now available.  Please log into your account on the Police Records Portal to view the records. The Records Division expects to provide the next installment of the Fusus/Axon Agreements/Contracts on or before September 23rd, 2026. 
Cordially, Police Public Disclosure Desk Redmond Police Department Police Records Portal

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: State of Jefferson, Federal Land Management & Rural Grievances — Bureau of Land Management Records (Northern California / Southern Oregon)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

I request all records maintained by the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) concerning the "State of Jefferson" movement and related rural/regional grievances about federal land management in northern California and southern Oregon (including Del Norte, Siskiyou, Modoc, Trinity, and Shasta counties in California and adjacent counties in southern Oregon). Specifically, I seek: (1) correspondence, petitions, resolutions, and public comments received by the BLM from counties, elected officials, or citizens referencing the "State of Jefferson," secession, or state-separation in connection with federal land-management policy; (2) records concerning county "coordination" requests, demands for greater local control over BLM-administered public lands, or disputes over grazing, mining, timber, water, or access in these areas that reference the State of Jefferson movement; (3) BLM responses, briefing papers, or internal analyses addressing the State of Jefferson movement or related land-use conflicts; and (4) records of public meetings or listening sessions where the State of Jefferson or secession was raised. Please provide records from 2013 to the present. Please search under the terms "State of Jefferson," "Jefferson," "secession," "coordination," "local control," "Del Norte," and "Cascadia." I am willing to accept records in electronic format.

Disclosure of the requested information is in the public interest because it will contribute significantly to public understanding of how federal public-lands management has intersected with state-separation sentiment in rural counties. This request is not made for commercial purposes; I will make the records freely available to the public and to scholars. This request satisfies the statutory public-interest fee-waiver standard.

If a full fee waiver is not granted, I request that fees be limited as I qualify as a representative of the news media and/or as an educational and noncommercial requester. Please notify me in advance if fees are expected to exceed $25.

Request for Expedited Processing: I request expedited processing on the basis of a compelling need. I certify that the statements in this request are true and correct to the best of my knowledge and belief.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Daniel Friedman

title: Robert Decker

communications.subject: Indiana Access to Public Records Act Request: Robert Decker
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Indiana Access to Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records related to the following current or former employees:

Robert Decker (6819-9836)

Hiring date, termination date, compensation, commendations, assignments/job roles, disciplinary actions, factual basis for disciplinary actions and letters of resignation for the following employees. Please exclude copies of individual training certificates.

I am including the following information as a helpful reference to related case law and Public Access Counselor opinions regarding personnel records of public employees:

https://public.courts.in.gov/Decisions/api/Document/Opinion?Id=QPNIyLTvnhzxDZhO52J1KCEs4fPOKpLR0hAitsADZUhV--IpFNWE224Cxiw0N3jJ0

Indiana Supreme Court decision WTHR-TV v. Hamilton Southeastern School District states that APRA requires disclosure of the factual basis for disciplinary action, and that factual basis cannot be a bald conclusion. It also has to be sufficient for a reasonable person to understand what an employee did to deserve discipline. See the opinion starting on page 7 of the link above.

A passing reference to violation of a specific policy is not sufficient to meet this standard.

The Indiana Public Access Counselor also has addressed the topic of resignations in lieu of termination. One such opinion can be reviewed here, but simply put a resignation in lieu of a termination does not dissolve an agency’s responsibility to provide the factual basis for discipline under the public records statute.

The state’s records statute applies to all employees, regardless of wither they are probationary or not.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 7 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Emily Hopkins

title: South Bay Regional Police Consortium (LA Area) - LexisNexis Data Sharing with Federal LE (Manhattan Beach Police Department)

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: South Bay Regional Police Consortium (LA Area) - LexisNexis Data Sharing with Federal LE (Manhattan Beach Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

We are working on an article focused on California police departments sharing local data with federal authorities, including ICE via LexisNexis. We identified your agency as part of a South Bay Regional Police Consortium that contracted with LexisNexis for AVCC in or around 2020. This request focuses on data your agency shares with LexisNexis, and interfaces that exist with your agency's RMS/CAD/JMS and LexisNexis's systems, including Accurint, Accurint Virtual Crime Center (AVCC), CommunityCrimeMap.com, or Public Safety Data Exchange (PSDEx)

We are requesting:
1) Technical integration documents: Any documents, integrations instructions, tutorials, and similar documents from LexisNexis about how to connect your RMS/CAD/JMS systems to LexisNexis's systems. [Typically held by IT or records systems teams/vendors from when your agency originally integrated with LexisNexis's systems]
2) Agreements: The signed "XML Addendum", Database Interface Agreement, or similar legal agreement that dictates how your agency's data may be used and shared. [Typically held by legal or procurement departments]
3) Shared Data: An export of what data you share with LexisNexis and other law enforcement agencies. This is often called a Data Classification Crime Results sheet. To obtain this, an account admin can click a link on the left-hand side under admin permissions called 'Data Classification Manager.' There is an Export link on the top right of the Data Classification Manager page. Depending on the LexisNexis product(s) you subscribe to, this may have a different name or location. We are looking for the list of data you share with LexisNexis, and who your share it with [Only an CCM/Accurint Account Administrators can access these documents]
4) Occasionally we have found consortiums who have negotiated to only share local data with other consortium members, not the 2,400 AVCC federal and local LE subscribers. If you have documentation that your data is only shared locally, please share it. Otherwise you may state there are no responsive documents to item 4. 

We welcome (but do not expect or request) any comments you have about the sharing of local police data with federal authorities via LexisNexis.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Shawn Segal

title: Steven Catron (Burlington Police Department)

communications.subject: Indiana Access to Public Records Act Request: Steven Catron (Burlington Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Indiana Access to Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records related to the following current or former employees:

Steven Catron (6303-1830)

Hiring date, termination date, compensation, commendations, assignments/job roles, disciplinary actions, factual basis for disciplinary actions and letters of resignation for the following employees. Please exclude copies of individual training certificates.

I am including the following information as a helpful reference to related case law and Public Access Counselor opinions regarding personnel records of public employees:

https://public.courts.in.gov/Decisions/api/Document/Opinion?Id=QPNIyLTvnhzxDZhO52J1KCEs4fPOKpLR0hAitsADZUhV--IpFNWE224Cxiw0N3jJ0

Indiana Supreme Court decision WTHR-TV v. Hamilton Southeastern School District states that APRA requires disclosure of the factual basis for disciplinary action, and that factual basis cannot be a bald conclusion. It also has to be sufficient for a reasonable person to understand what an employee did to deserve discipline. See the opinion starting on page 7 of the link above.

A passing reference to violation of a specific policy is not sufficient to meet this standard.

The Indiana Public Access Counselor also has addressed the topic of resignations in lieu of termination. One such opinion can be reviewed here, but simply put a resignation in lieu of a termination does not dissolve an agency’s responsibility to provide the factual basis for discipline under the public records statute.

The state’s records statute applies to all employees, regardless of wither they are probationary or not.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 7 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Emily Hopkins

communications.subject: Alabama Open Records Law Request: Complete Code of Alabama — bulk machine-readable copy
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Alabama Open Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

This is a public-records request for the complete enacted text of the Code of Alabama, all titles and chapters, current through the most recent session, in bulk machine-readable form. Three items, all requested:

1. NOW — the consolidated machine-readable source file the State already maintains (XML, database export, or word-processing files). Enacted statutory text only; no publisher annotations.

2. GOING FORWARD — the recurring updated export after each session. In the alternative, and preferably: simply PUBLISH the complete bulk code file as a free public download on the State's own site, once and for all.

3. THE PUBLISHING ARRANGEMENT — any contract/MOU/license between the State and any commercial publisher governing the Code, plus the technical exhibits (format, frequency, delivery method). Administrative/procurement records.

Legal basis: enacted statutes are public-domain government edicts (Georgia v. Public.Resource.Org). Electronic delivery only. If you are not the custodian, please identify who is.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

André Natta, a citizen of Alabama, in coordination with GavelSight.

communications.subject: Copy of Code of Alabama
communications.communication:
Mr. Natta,

I am in receipt of your letter dated July 16, 2026, wherein you request a copy of the text of the compete enacted Code of Alabama.

We do not keep a copy of the entire code in a single document or database export, but we do make the entire text of the Alabama code available on our website: www.legislature.state.al.us<http://www.legislature.state.al.us/>. If you click on "Legal Resources" and then on the next page click "Code of Alabama" that will take you to the code directory.  From there you can select any one section of code and select print.  Once you've selected "print" it will allow you to select the entire code for printing to a printer or saving to PDF on your computer.

Alternatively, although I'm not an expert in this field, the following link has details on how to fetch the Code of Alabama text.  As I understand it, you can programmatically grab the code text from the website. I believe you would just need to look at the API for the Code found on this page: https://alison.legislature.state.al.us/api.  This involves paginating through the whole code, grabbing the Sections and extracting the text from those records (preferrable for a program or script to do this for you).  We have no single request that will return the entire Code of Alabama, but you should be able to construct it using the info available on the public API site.

title: Retail food facility roster and inspection data (Ventura County, CA)

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Retail food facility roster and inspection data (Ventura County, CA)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

To the Records Officer, Ventura County Environmental Health Division (Resource Management Agency):

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act (Gov. Code § 7920.000 et seq.), I request copies of the following records in electronic format:

1. The current roster of all active retail food facility permits maintained by your agency, including for each facility, to the extent maintained: facility name and DBA, site address, mailing address, owner or operator name, phone number, permit type or program/risk classification, and permit status with effective dates.

2. Retail food facility inspection results from 2024-08-06 through the date this request is processed, including for each inspection: the facility identifier or name and address, inspection date, inspection type, score or grade where used, and the violation codes and descriptions cited.

Both categories are maintained in your environmental health data system and are routinely produced by comparable agencies as spreadsheet exports. Per Gov. Code § 7922.575, I request the records in any electronic format in which they already exist — CSV, Excel, or a database export is preferred over PDF, and no new record needs to be created to comply.

If any portion of a record is exempt, please release the remainder with the exempt portion redacted (§ 7922.525) and cite the specific exemption relied upon. If duplication fees apply, please provide an itemized estimate of the direct cost of duplication in advance (§ 7922.530); for electronic records we expect this to be minimal or zero.

Thank you for your assistance.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Benjamin Conn

title: Flock Safety ALPR Use Across Union County, NJ — Audit Logs, Searches & Data Sharing (Municipal Clerk)

communications.subject: New Jersey Open Public Records Act Request: Flock Safety ALPR Use Across Union County, NJ — Audit Logs, Searches & Data Sharing (Municipal Clerk)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the New Jersey Open Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

For the period July 20, 2026 through August 19, 2026, please provide:

1. Records showing the total number of license plates, vehicle detections, or plate reads captured or scanned through Flock Safety ALPR systems accessible to or operated by the department.

2. The names of all hot lists, watch lists, alert lists, or similar lists used, enabled, or accessible through the department’s Flock Safety system.

3. A list of all law enforcement agencies, government entities, organizations, or other entities with which the department shares Flock Safety ALPR data.

4. A list of all law enforcement agencies, government entities, organizations, or other entities from which the department receives or has access to Flock Safety ALPR data.

5. All agreements, memoranda of understanding, contracts, arrangements, or other records concerning access to Flock Safety cameras, systems, or data owned, funded, or operated by homeowner associations, private businesses, private organizations, or individuals.

6. All current contracts, memoranda of understanding, agreements, amendments, renewals, statements of work, or similar agreements between the department, municipality, or other applicable public entity and Flock Safety.

7. All procurement records related to Flock Safety, including purchase orders, invoices, bids, quotes, proposals, requisitions, payment records, and records reflecting the purchase, lease, subscription, acquisition, installation, or renewal of Flock Safety equipment or services.

8. All audit logs, search logs, query logs, usage reports, or similar records relating to the department’s use of Flock Safety ALPR systems during the requested period, including but not limited to:

- Records of license plate or vehicle searches performed by agency personnel;
- Dates and timestamps of searches;
- User identification associated with searches, including names, badge numbers, usernames, or user IDs, where maintained;
- Case numbers, incident numbers, investigation references, reasons, or purposes associated with searches, where maintained;
- Records showing networks or agencies whose Flock data is shared with or accessible to the department;
- Records showing networks or agencies to which the department shares its Flock data;
- Event logs, system activity logs, or audit records reflecting changes to hot lists, watch lists, alerts, users, permissions, or network-sharing settings;
- Records showing changes to data-sharing relationships or network access; and
- Records reflecting live-stream, live-view, camera access, or similar access permissions and configuration settings, if applicable.

This request specifically includes records available through Flock Safety features or reports identified as “Organization Audit,” “Network Audit,” or equivalent audit, usage, sharing, or administrative reports available within the Flock Safety platform, including the “Insights” section where applicable.

9. Records showing the department’s current Flock Safety network-sharing configuration, including which networks, agencies, or organizations share data with the department and which networks, agencies, or organizations receive data from the department.

10. Screenshots, exports, reports, or other existing records reflecting relevant Flock Safety configuration settings, including network-sharing settings and live-stream/live-view access settings, to the extent such records are maintained by the agency.

Please provide responsive records in their original electronic format where reasonably available. For databases, audit logs, search logs, reports, or tabular records, I prefer CSV, XLS/XLSX, or another native machine-readable format rather than PDF printouts.

This request seeks existing government records and does not require the agency to create a new record. If a requested list or summary does not exist as a standalone record, please provide the existing report, export, audit log, configuration record, or other record containing the requested information.

In advance of filing this request, Flock Safety was consulted regarding the availability of these records. Flock Safety indicated that if an agency administrator has difficulty locating relevant audit or system records, the administrator may contact Flock Safety for support.

If any portion of a responsive record is considered exempt from disclosure, please redact only the exempt portion and provide the remainder of the record. Please identify the specific legal basis for each withholding or redaction.

The requested records will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

Thank you for your assistance.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 7 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Madthew Pierre-Louis

communications.subject: Nevada Public Records Act Request: Library Contract Request: EBSCO Academic Search Premier (College Of Southern Nevada)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Nevada Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1) The most recent contract, governing, base, or master license agreement with EBSCO, relating to the product Academic Search Premier;
2) All related terms and conditions, terms of service, amendments, addenda, appendices, attachments, product terms, MOUs, MOAs, data processing agreements, and/or letters of intent; and
3) All financial documents or records of financial transactions, exchanges or obligations related to contractual relations with EBSCO for Academic Search Premier. 

Please do not limit your search to strictly direct agreements or renewals between the institution and EBSCO, but include all agreements and related documentation through consortia such as a state or regional library consortium (such as the Greater Western Library Alliance) or Lyrasis.

Responsive materials include all contracts, agreements, amendments, appendices, invoices, and any other documents listed above that incorporate language governing terms of use of Academic Search Premier.

We are an alliance of academic research librarians conducting critical research on library vendor contract terminology related to data privacy to identify and expose significant disparities in language between vendors and institutions. This research is essential for advancing national awareness and advocacy around library patron data privacy rights. We would be grateful for your cooperation in supporting this important initiative.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Illinois Freedom of Information Act., I hereby request the following records:

The documents I am seeking include, but are not limited to:

Records of Chicago Police Department dispatch including but not limited to the following fields: 
- event number
- event date
- dispatched
- enroute
- onscene
- priority
- district #
- disposition
- xcoord
- ycoord
- badge #

Scope: Police Districts 11, 12, 14, 25 
Timeframe: Sunday, August 23rd, 2026, from 16:00 - 20:00

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

ll

title: Sunshine Law Request: Precythe

communications.subject: The Missouri Sunshine Law Request: Sunshine Law Request: Precythe
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the The Missouri Sunshine Law, I hereby request the following records:

All email communications where Anne L. Precythe is either the sender, recipient, CC'ed, or BCC'ed, sent between the dates of 1/1/2022 and 10/12/2023 and containing at least one of the following keywords: "Talitrix", "electronic monitoring" or "contract." Please include any variations that are not case sensitive. Please include all email attachments.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

e

In the meantime, if you have any questions please let me know.

Sincerely,


Matt Briesacher
Office of the General Counsel

Missouri Department of Corrections
2729 Plaza Drive
Jefferson City, MO 65109

Office: (573) 526-6504

NOTICE:  This electronic mail message and any attachments may contain attorney-client privileged or otherwise confidential information.  Recipients should ensure that proper security measures are taken to maintain any privileged or confidential information.  If you are not an intended recipient of this electronic mail message as listed above, please notify my office immediately and delete or destroy the electronic message and all printed copies.  The unauthorized disclosure of privileged or otherwise confidential information is strictly prohibited.  All recipients are hereby notified that (1) electronic mail is not secure, (2) any electronic mail sent to or received by you may be exposed to multiple computers and/or users in transit, and (3) interception during transit by improper access may occur. Please contact us immediately if you do not want this office to communicate with you by e-mail. Thank you.

communications.subject: RE: The Missouri Sunshine Law Request: Sunshine Law Request: Precythe
communications.communication:
Good Morning.  We received the results for the e-mail search you requested and the results captured 5340 e-mails.  Based on a very quick review, it appears that the term “contract” is the source of many of the hits.  There are also many closed records in the results – for instance e-mails from the department’s medical contract monitor team that contain health information on individual offenders.  With the press of other business, this review will take some time so I thought it might be prudent to ask if you would want to remove “contract” from the search terms to narrow the results.   I hope that makes sense and if you would like us to review all the results as the request was submitted, we will certainly do that.

If you have any questions, please let me know.

Sincerely,


Matt Briesacher
Office of the General Counsel

Missouri Department of Corrections
2729 Plaza Drive
Jefferson City, MO 65109

Office: (573) 526-6504

title: US Navy support for NASCAR 2026 San Diego Weekend

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: US Navy support for NASCAR 2026 San Diego Weekend
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

All documents pertaining to collaboration between the US Navy and the TV production of NASCAR 2026 San Diego Weekend. Such documents may include but should not be limited to: script notes; production assistance agreements; photographs; and all records of communications between employees of the Navy and members of the cast, crew, and production company of NASCAR 2026 San Diego Weekend, including memos, notes of meetings and conference calls, emails, and other forms of communication.

NASCAR 2026 San Diego Weekend appears (as "NASCAR 2026 San Diego Weekend [Amazon Prime streaming, FS1 network and CW network]") in a list of Navy-supported productions for the year 2025 that was released to me through FOIA. That list is attached to this request.

I am the Director of Research Operations at a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization called The Decoding Culture Foundation as well as the editor-in-chief and a contributor to a research magazine published by said foundation titled "Cultural Engineering Studies." These documents will be used for public education and research purposes. I therefore request a waiver of all fees that may otherwise apply. Attached is a document with organization letterhead confirming my position, as well as the organization's 501(c)(3) application and approval form.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Brett Carollo

communications.subject: Navy FOIA Request 2026-NavyFOIA-007506 - Acknowledgment
communications.communication:
Dear Mr. Carollo: 

The Department of the Navy received your Freedom of Information (FOIA) / Privacy Act (PA) request dated 4 May 2026 and placed it in queue for processing by order of receipt on 4 May 2026. 

Unusual circumstances arise when a response within the statutory 20-day period may not be attainable due to: 

1. Collection and search for records from a facility outside of this office. 
2. Volume of records that may be responsive to your request. 
3. Consultation with one or more agencies having a substantial interest in the determination or the subject matter. 

The Navy FOIA program is decentralized, requiring our office to search and gather documents from Navy component offices which are not geographically co-located. Per the Department of the Navy FOIA/PA regulation 32 CFR §701.8(g)(2), this office grants itself an extension of ten days response time. We appreciate your patience and understand the importance of timely responses to FOIA requests and apologize for any inconvenience this delay may cause. 

Additionally, please be aware that the U.S. Navy’s new FOIA portal, Secure Release, is online. For your convenience, you may now submit FOIA requests online at www.SecureRelease.us or www.FOIA.gov. 

Please direct questions to the FOIA Service Center by phone (202) 685-0412 or send via email don-foia-pa@us.navy.mil. 

U.S. Navy Headquarters (FOIA)

title: City of Glenpool Opioid Settlement Funds

communications.subject: Oklahoma Open Records Act Request: City of Glenpool Opioid Settlement Funds
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Under the Oklahoma Open Records Act, 51 §24A.1 et seq., I request an opportunity to inspect or obtain copies of public records related to the allocation and use of opioid lawsuit settlement funds in the City of Glenpool. Specifically, I am seeking:

1. Documentation of the amount of opioid settlement funds your office has received thus far from the Oklahoma Attorney General’s Office as a non-litigating political subdivision. 
2. Records detailing which individuals and/or programs have been awarded a portion of your opioid lawsuit settlement funds. 
3. Any documentation related to the review or approval process to apply for funding, including the names and organizations of individuals involved in the application process. 
4. Minutes of any public meetings or hearings, including public officials, in which opioid settlement fund allocation was discussed. 
5. Any correspondence and attachments between county officials regarding the allocation or use of these funds. 

If there are any fees for searching or copying these records, please inform me if the cost will exceed $25.00. However, I would also like to request a waiver of all fees, as disclosure of the requested information is in the public interest. This request is related to news-gathering purposes; it is not being sought for commercial purposes.

If you expect a significant delay in responding to or in fulfilling this request, please contact me with information about when I might expect copies or the ability to inspect the requested records.

I look forward to receiving your response to this request. Thank you for the help, and please let me know if you have any questions. 

Sincerely, 

Sierra Pfeifer | KOSU
Mental health & addiction reporter
sierra@kosu.org | 919-448-5430

Greetings We are pleased to inform you that we have completed work on the above-referenced FOIA request. title: Information Regarding RCW 9.94A.030 §36 (Department of Corrections)

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: Information Regarding RCW 9.94A.030 §36 (Department of Corrections)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Unless otherwise specified, I am requesting data covering the five-year period through the date of this request.

For purposes of this request, "gang enhancement" refers to the sentencing enhancement applied under RCW 9.94A.533(8) to offenses qualifying as "criminal street gang-related offenses" as defined in RCW 9.94A.030(14), involving defendants qualifying as "criminal street gang associates or members" as defined in RCW 9.94A.030(13), and involving a "pattern of criminal street gang activity" as defined in RCW 9.94A.030(36).
1. The total number of individuals charged with a criminal street gang-related offense under RCW 9.94A.030(14), or against whom a gang sentencing enhancement under RCW 9.94A.533(8) was alleged, broken down by year for the past five years.
2. The racial and gender demographics of all individuals charged with a criminal street gang-related offense or gang enhancement under the above provisions during that period, disaggregated by year to the extent available.
3. Conviction rates for individuals charged with a gang-related offense or against whom a gang enhancement was alleged, including the number and percentage of cases resolved by conviction, acquittal, dismissal, or other disposition, broken down by year.
4. The number of individuals currently in Washington Department of Corrections (DOC) custody whose sentence includes a gang enhancement imposed under RCW 9.94A.533(8).
5. The number of cases over the past five years in which a gang enhancement under RCW 9.94A.533(8) was included in the initial charging or sentencing documentation but was subsequently not imposed as part of a negotiated plea or sentencing agreement, broken down by year.
6. The average sentence length in cases where a gang enhancement under RCW 9.94A.533(8) was dropped or reduced through a plea or sentencing agreement, compared with the average sentence length in cases where the enhancement was imposed at sentencing, broken down by year to the extent available.
7. The age distribution — including mean age, median age, and full age range — of individuals charged with a gang-related offense or against whom a gang enhancement was alleged under the above provisions, over the past five years.
8. The average total sentence length for the underlying predicate offense alone, compared with the average total sentence for the underlying offense combined with the gang enhancement under RCW 9.94A.533(8), for cases resolved during the past five years.
9. The number of cases in which a gang enhancement under RCW 9.94A.533(8) was applied involving: (a) juveniles tried as adults in superior court following a decline hearing under RCW 13.40.110; or (b) defendants whose cases originated in juvenile court proceedings under Title 13 RCW, over the past five years.
10. For defendants against whom a gang enhancement under RCW 9.94A.533(8) was alleged over the past five years: the number represented by the Office of Public Defense or county public defender versus private counsel, along with corresponding conviction rates and average sentence lengths for each group.
11. The number of gang enhancement cases under RCW 9.94A.533(8) prosecuted by county, broken down by year, for the past five years.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jenny Wadhwa

title: Town Take‑Home Vehicles and Taxable Fringe Benefits

communications.subject: New York Freedom of Information Law Request: Town Take‑Home Vehicles and Taxable Fringe Benefits
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the New York Freedom of Information Law, I hereby request the following records:

Copies of records from January 1, 2022 through the present relating to town‑owned vehicles assigned to employees as take‑home or personally assigned vehicles.
Please provide the following categories of records, in any format in which they are maintained (paper or electronic), and from any department that maintains them:

Vehicle assignments
*Any lists, inventories, or other records identifying town‑owned vehicles assigned to individual employees for take‑home or personally assigned use, including: vehicle year/make/model, VIN, department, and the name and title of the assigned employee, with dates of assignment and, if applicable, return or reassignment.

Usage / mileage records
*Any records showing the odometer reading or total accumulated mileage for each town‑owned vehicle assigned as a take‑home or personally assigned vehicle, as of the most recent date available.
*Mileage logs, trip sheets, vehicle use logs, GPS/telematics reports, or similar records showing business, commuting, or other personal use of those vehicles.
*Any forms or reports employees submit to document personal or commuting use of employer‑provided vehicles for payroll or tax purposes.

Payroll / taxable fringe benefit records
*Payroll, accounting, or other records that show taxable fringe benefit amounts attributed to employees’ personal or commuting use of town‑owned take‑home vehicles and included in their wages, such as payroll registers, year‑to‑date taxable fringe benefit totals, W‑2 support, or similar records.
*Any records indicating the method used to value this fringe benefit (for example, cents‑per‑mile, annual lease value, or commuting valuation), consistent with IRS Publication 15‑B or related IRS guidance on employer‑provided vehicles.

Policies and reviews
*Any written policies, procedures, or internal guidance on the assignment, use, or personal/commuting use of town‑owned vehicles.
*Any audit reports, management letters, or internal reviews since January 1, 2022 that address take‑home vehicles, vehicle use recordkeeping, or reporting of taxable fringe benefits for employer‑provided vehicles.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Michael McCall

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Florida Sunshine Law, I hereby request the following records:

I am currently seeking updated quarterly performance data from your plan’s alternative asset holdings for the following date(s): 1Q20, 2Q20, 3Q20, 4Q20, 1Q21, 2Q21, 3Q21, 4Q21, 1Q26 & 2Q26.

1.	Names and vintage years of all private equity, venture capital, mezzanine, distressed, real estate/REIT, debt and infrastructure partnerships in City of Kissimmee Municipal Firefighters' Retirement Plan's portfolio.

11.	For each fund, please indicate whether or not the fund uses Subscription Credit Facilities.
I also request a copy of any disclosable documents which contain some or all of the following information:
12.	Names of all hedge fund holdings (including hedge fund of funds) in City of Kissimmee Municipal Firefighters' Retirement Plan's portfolio.

Dear Jen Anderson,

Thank you for the general ledger entries provided on August 31, 2026. While the District has provided basic accounting records proving Check No. 415420 was processed, the response remains non-compliant with the full scope of the request under the Washington Public Records Act (PRA). I object to the administrative closure of this request based on the following deficiencies:

1. Item 1 (Line-Item Billing Sheets): Page 19 contains only a flat summary sheet referencing a block of 30.0 hours. Under Progressive Animal Welfare Society (PAWS) v. University of Washington, 125 Wash. 2d 243 (1994), attorney billing sheets and time blocks documenting public expenditures are public records subject to disclosure. Please produce the actual itemized time logs, dates, and detailed line-item billing entries submitted by McMinimee Law to justify the $10,500 total expenditure.

2. Item 2 (Over-Redaction of Settlement Agreement): Pages 8, 9, and 10 of the produced settlement contract are entirely blacked out. Under Soter v. Cowles Publishing Co., 162 Wash. 2d 716 (2007) and RCW 42.56.210(1), blanket page-level withholdings are structurally unlawful. While the District must redact specific student-identifiable elements protected by FERPA, it is legally required to segment the record, leaving the systemic contractual terms, general operational agreements, and non-identifiable text fully visible. 

Please provide a revised, properly parsed production of the settlement agreement and the missing detailed time logs to satisfy this request.

Respectfully Submitted in the Public Interest,

Public Interest Mainstreaming Parenting

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: CVISS Member Agencies - LexisNexis/Accurint Data Sharing Agreements (Elk Grove Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1) All MOUs, contracts, addendums, or other legal documents signed by your agency and LexisNexis (and subsidiaries, including LexisNexis Risk Solutions, Accurint, AVCC, PSDEX, etc.). This may include (but is not limited to) a LexisNexis Consortium Sub-Agency Addendum, Schedule A, or other agreements.
2) Any MOUs or other agreements between your agency and CVISS or Sacramento County Sheriff related to sharing RMS/CAD data.
3) Agency Configuration Page: A printout of your agency's AVCC configuration page. Please include the full page, including any other agencies listed on the same page. Example Screenshot: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1G_J35fnmu7qZO_k8UOoVHFcd_R2HKXVg/view?usp=sharing

Context: We understand that CVISS moved to the LexisNexis Accurint platform to share data among CVISS member agencies. We are seeking to understand whether your agency and other CVISS members share contributed data with agencies beyond the consortium (e.g., the Public Safety Data Exchange / PSDEX national database), or whether data sharing is restricted to CVISS members only. Often LexisNexis Sub-Agency Addendums allow agencies to choose whether they share nationally or only within the consortium - we seek to understand what your agency chose to do.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Shawn Segal

I wanted to follow up on the following Freedom of Information Act request, copied below, and originally submitted on March 24, 2026. Please let me know when I can expect to receive a response.

Thanks for your help, and let me know if further clarification is needed.

communications.subject: Your Request to Treasury 2026-FOIA-01299
communications.communication:
Greetings, 
Please find the Department of the Treasury's Acknowledgment of your Freedom of Information Act request 2026-FOIA-01299, attached. 
The FOIA Requester Service Center can be reached at FOIA@treasury.gov. Please reference FOIA case number 2026-FOIA-01299 when contacting our office about this request if any questions arise. (mailto:FOIA@treasury.gov) 
Sincerely, 
Department of the Treasury

communications.subject: FOIA Auto-Reply
communications.communication:
[cid:image001.jpg@01D0A2E1.4C3000A0]

The U.S. Department of the Treasury has received the information you submitted to the FOIA@TREASURY.gov<mailto:FOIA@TREASURY.gov>  mailbox.

If you are submitting a FOIA request, this courtesy reply does not replace the acknowledgement letter which will include a FOIA case number once your request has been entered into our FOIA Request Tracking System.

If you are seeking the status of a pending FOIA request for which you have a FOIA case number, please call (202) 622-0930 to obtain the status of your request.

Please visit our FOIA Library at http://www.treasury.gov/FOIA/Pages/reading_room.aspx.

Thank you for contacting the U.S. Department of the Treasury.

communications.subject: Final Response for Department of the Treasury OIG FOIA Request 2026-FOIA-01299
communications.communication:
Dear Mr. Segal:

Attached please find Treasury Office of Inspector General's final response to your Freedom of Information Act request, referenced as 2026-FOIA-01299.

Sincerely,

FOIA -Treasury Office of Inspector General

_______________
Looking for Treasury OIG reports (Audits, Investigations, Peer Review, Semi-Annual Reports to Congress) or testimonies and other documents? Find them, publicly available on the Treasury website, here:  https://oig.treasury.gov/other-reports-testimonies.

Want to submit a FOIA request for Treasury OIG records not located on the above website? Please go here: https://foia.treasury.gov/app/Home.aspx.



"This message and any attachment(s) may contain restricted, sensitive, and/or controlled unclassified information belonging to the US Department of the Treasury, Office of Inspector General. It is not for release, review, retransmission, dissemination, or use by anyone other than the intended recipient. If you received this communication in error, please immediately notify the sender and delete or destroy this communication and all attachments."
